title: The locally quaternion group is a countable $B$-group
summary: A group $G$ is a $B$-group if every primitive permutation group containing a regular subgroup isomorphic to $G$ is doubly transitive. We prove that the locally quaternion group $\mathrm{Dic}(C_{2^\infty},c)$, the extension of the Prüfer $2$-group by an element squaring to its involution and inverting it, is a $B$-group. This gives an example of a countably infinite $B$-group. This answers Problem 13.30 of the Kourovka Notebook.
